title: Adaptive experimentation controller: metrics gates, soft-shutdown and safe fallback policy
author: Ravi Kapoor
release_notes: Adds the Adaptive Experimentation Controller: metric-gated canaries, automatic soft-shutdown, and deterministic fallback policy. Backwards compatible with existing rollout configs. Deploy with safety gates enabled by default for new experiments.
description:
Context: we need a single, testable control plane for running short-duration experiments (canaries, A/B splits, and shadow runs) that enforces safety gates based on observed metrics and can gracefully and deterministically shut down an experiment if thresholds are breached. Motivation: prior rollouts relied on ad-hoc workflows and separate operators; incidents in Q4 showed slow rollbacks when latency regressions or hallucination rate spikes occurred. This PR introduces an Adaptive Experimentation Controller (AEC) that centralizes rollout decisions, exposes a policy-language for metric gates, and implements a soft-shutdown sequence that preserves in-flight requests and drains prefixes to avoid KV cache invalidations.

Design summary: the AEC is implemented as a controller in pkg/orchestrator with three primary components: (1) policy-engine: evaluates metric windows and decides PASS/WARN/FAIL per experiment; (2) controller-loop: phases traffic (0->mirror->phased-canary->full) using token-aware sampling and deterministic hashing; (3) safe-shutdown: a soft-stop path that 1) immediately disables new canary allocations, 2) flips traffic to fallback model variant for new requests, and 3) drains existing sessions with an adjustable grace window. Key invariants: decisions are idempotent, metric windows are sampled from the centralized metrics store (observability-pack), and fallback mapping is explicit in rollout spec to avoid implicit fallthroughs.

Config changes: new CRD-like rollout spec additions in api/v1/experiment.go: "metricsGates" (list), "graceWindowSeconds", and "fallbackPolicy" (enum: degrade|fallback-model|region-redirect). Default behavior keeps legacy rollouts unchanged unless the new fields are supplied. The CLI (rdwctl rollout apply) accepts --enable-aec flag for early rollout in staging clusters.

Testing and validation: unit tests for policy evaluation and deterministic hashing (pkg/orchestrator/policy_engine_test.go) added. Integration test harness uses benchmark-lab to simulate 100k qps with mixed sequence lengths and synthetic hallucination signals to trigger gate states. A small e2e in redwood-quickstarts demonstrates staged activation with dashboards in redwood-console (observability/dashboard.json example). Performance: local bench shows <2% p95 latency overhead at 1k qps when metric evaluation is on-path; objective is to push evaluation off-path for large clusters in follow-up PR.

Migration and rollout plan: opt-in feature gate (aec.alpha.redwood.io) enabled on staging. Plan: deploy controller to staging, run 2 weeks of canaries for internal traffic, then enable for early customers with explicit opt-in. If a gate FAILs, the controller performs soft-shutdown and posts a structured incident event to incident-bot with rollback suggested. Owners must validate fallback mapping before enabling for production.

Docs and observability: added docs/experiments/adaptive-controller.md and a monitoring playbook describing gate metrics (latency_p95_delta, token_error_rate, hallucination_rate_est). Console graphs for experiment state transitions and a per-experiment timeline have been added.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear (ENG-7812) - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] e2e quickstart example - [x] Docs & monitoring dashboards - [x] Feature gate behind "aec.alpha.redwood.io"

Risks and mitigations: the policy engine is conservative by default (WARN -> requires manual confirm) and FAIL triggers soft-shutdown not an immediate hard rollback. The first rollout uses a short graceWindowSeconds=30 to limit long-lived sessions. Next steps: move metric evaluation to a sidecar aggregator and add automatic rollback reasons to audit logs.

review_conversation: Ava Martinez (reviewer): Overall nice clean split. Question: how do we guarantee cache-affinity when we do a fallback-model redirect? Suggest we add a KV prefix map to the fallback step.
Ravi Kapoor (author): Good point — added a fallbackPrefix map and updated controller.go to preserve prefix affinity during soft-shutdown. See commit b2d8e3f.
Jordan Li (reviewer): CI flaked on the integration test (benchmark scenario) — looks like a race while the metrics source is being torn down. Can you add a retry/backoff?
Ravi Kapoor (author): Added retry with exponential backoff and a short jitter; test stabilized locally and in CI.
